faqs.question: What is the Reichert 4SPR used for?
faqs.answer: It's a four-channel surface plasmon resonance system for real-time, label-free measurement of biomolecular binding kinetics and affinity.

faqs.question: How sensitive is the Reichert 4SPR?
faqs.answer: It detects interactions with low molecular weight compounds down to roughly 100 Da, across an affinity range from 1 mM to 1 pM.

faqs.question: Can the Reichert 4SPR run crude, unpurified samples?
faqs.answer: Yes, it runs whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates directly, without a purification step first.

faqs.question: How long does a tubing change take?
faqs.answer: About five minutes, using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, without needing a service call.

faqs.question: Do the flow cells need to be replaced regularly?
faqs.answer: No, flow cells clean or swap by hand and aren't treated as a disposable cartridge.

faqs.question: Is a service contract required?
faqs.answer: No, the open design allows in-house maintenance of the parts that typically need attention, though a service contract remains available as an option.

faqs.question: What sensor chips are available?
faqs.answer: Carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, plain gold, and specialized chips for custom applications.

faqs.question: How many samples can run per experiment?
faqs.answer: Up to 768 samples per run.

faqs.question: How is the 4SPR different from the 2SPR and 3SPR?
faqs.answer: The 4SPR offers four channels and up to three simultaneous experiments, while the 3SPR and 2SPR scale down channel count and throughput for labs with lower parallel testing needs, at a correspondingly lower cost of entry.

Reichert 4SPR opens everything up: swap tubing in five minutes, clean the flow cell yourself, run crude samples without purifying them first. Four channels mean up to three simultaneous experiments, sensitivity down to roughly 100 Da, industry-leading low drift at 0.1 μRIU/min, and sample capacity up to 768 runs. sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Reichert 4SPR product information: channel configuration, sensitivity specs, and open-system serviceability.
body: Four channels run up to three experiments at once, speeding up method development by testing different immobilization chemistries or regeneration schemes side by side.

Sensitivity reaches low molecular weight compounds down to roughly 100 Da, supporting affinity measurements from 1 mM to 1 pM, precise thermodynamic parameter determination, and accurate concentration analysis.
Drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min with noise as low as 0.05 μRIU rms, and baseline stabilizes 2 to 3x faster than competing systems thanks to streamlined fluidics.
Sample capacity reaches up to 768 samples per run.
The system is genuinely open: tubing changes in five minutes using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, and flow cells clean or swap by hand rather than requiring a cartridge replacement.
Crude samples run directly, whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates, without a purification step first.

A full range of standard sensor chips ships alongside the system: carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, and plain gold for custom chemistry.
No service contract is required to keep the system running. Accessible parts mean routine maintenance happens in-house, though a service contract remains available for labs that prefer it.

sections.title: Four Channels, Flexible Experiment Design
sections.description: A single-channel system forces experiments into a queue. Four channels turn that queue into parallel throughput, running different immobilization chemistries or regeneration schemes side by side instead of one after another.
body: That flexibility isn't fixed to one layout. Configurations include three experimental channels against one shared reference, two experimental channels with their own separate references, four channels running as two independent pairs, or the same pairs run at different times entirely.
For labs that don't need that level of throughput, two-channel and three-channel Reichert systems cover the same open, low-cost design at a smaller scale.

faqs.question: What is the Reichert 3SPR used for?
faqs.answer: It's a three-channel surface plasmon resonance system for real-time, label-free measurement of biomolecular binding kinetics and affinity, built to balance throughput and cost.

faqs.question: How sensitive is the Reichert 3SPR?
faqs.answer: It detects interactions with low molecular weight compounds under 100 Da, across an affinity range from 1 mM to 1 pM.

faqs.question: How much does the Reichert 3SPR save compared to competitors?
faqs.answer: It typically costs 20% less than a lower-throughput system from the leading competitor, and a typical lab saves around $20,000 per year per system, roughly $100,000 over five years.

faqs.question: Can the Reichert 3SPR run crude, unpurified samples?
faqs.answer: Yes, it runs whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates directly, without a purification step first.

faqs.question: How long does a tubing change take?
faqs.answer: About five minutes, using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, without needing a service call.

faqs.question: Do the flow cells need to be replaced regularly?
faqs.answer: No, flow cells clean or swap by hand and aren't treated as a disposable cartridge.

faqs.question: Is a service contract required?
faqs.answer: No, the open design allows in-house maintenance of the parts that typically need attention, though a service contract remains available as an option.

faqs.question: What sensor chips are available?
faqs.answer: Carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, plain gold, and specialized chips for custom applications.

faqs.question: How is the 3SPR different from the 2SPR and 4SPR?
faqs.answer: The 3SPR offers three channels and up to two simultaneous experiments, sitting between the 2SPR's lower-cost, lower-throughput format and the 4SPR's higher-throughput, four-channel design.

longForm.heroHook: Three channels. Two experiments at once. The sweet spot between throughput and cost.
longForm.heroLead: Two channels can feel limiting. Four can feel like paying for capacity you don't need. Reichert 3SPR sits right in the middle: immobilize different molecules on two channels while a third stays as reference, maximizing data output without the price tag of a full four-channel system, all while costing 20% less than a lower-throughput system from the leading competitor. Sensitivity reaches below 100 Da, affinity measurement spans 1 mM to 1 pM, drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min, and the same open, self-serviceable design that defines the Reichert line keeps ongoing costs low too.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Reichert 3SPR product information: channel flexibility, sensitivity specs, and open-system serviceability.
body: Three channels run up to two experiments at once, letting different immobilization chemistries or regeneration schemes get tested in parallel instead of one after another.

Sensitivity reaches low molecular weight compounds under 100 Da, supporting high-quality kinetic analysis, affinity measurements from 1 mM to 1 pM, precise thermodynamic parameter determination, and accurate concentration analysis.
Drift sits at an industry-leading 0.1 μRIU/min with noise as low as 0.05 μRIU rms, and baseline stabilizes 2 to 3x faster than competing systems thanks to streamlined fluidics.
Sample capacity reaches up to 768 samples per run.
The system is fully open: tubing changes in five minutes using standard, off-the-shelf HPLC fittings, and flow cells clean or swap by hand rather than requiring a cartridge replacement.
Crude samples run directly, whole cells, viruses, lysates, serum, and aggregates, without a purification step first.

A full range of standard sensor chips ships alongside the system: carboxymethyl dextran, planar PEG/carboxyl, nickel NTA, hydrophobic planar alkyl, streptavidin/NeutrAvidin, protein A, and plain gold for custom chemistry.
No service contract is required to keep the system running. Accessible parts mean routine maintenance happens in-house, though a service contract remains available for labs that prefer it.

sections.title: Open System, Real Savings
sections.description: SPR platforms that lock parts behind a service contract turn routine maintenance into a recurring, unpredictable cost. Reichert 3SPR puts the parts that need attention directly in reach. Purchasing the system typically costs 20% less than a lower-throughput system from the leading competitor, and a typical lab saves around $20,000 per year per system, roughly $100,000 over five years. Tubing uses standard HPLC fittings, changeable in five minutes without waiting on a service call, and compatible with a wide range of sample viscosities and particulate matter. Flow cells clean by hand and aren't treated as a disposable cartridge, unlike systems that require replacement once or twice a year. Sensor chips run at often less than half the price of comparable chips elsewhere, meaningful given a typical lab burns through 75 to 200 chips annually. None of this requires a service contract to access. A contract remains available, but it's a choice, not a condition of ownership.

sections.title: Three Channels, Flexible Experiment Design
sections.description: A single-channel system forces experiments into a queue. Three channels open up parallel throughput without the cost of a full four-channel platform.
body: That flexibility covers several layouts: two experimental channels against one shared reference, useful for testing an analyte's binding to multiple targets at once, one experimental channel run against two different references, or two paired runs executed at different times using the same reference.
For labs that need even more parallel capacity, a four-channel system scales further. For labs that need less, a two-channel system covers the same open, low-cost design at a smaller scale.
